claim.pdf_says: Under '5) For each parameter that is passed by value there shall be a corresponding parameter in the invoked method that:' the subitems are printed as separate list items - 'a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase' (end of the preceding page) and, at the top of this page, 'b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly.'
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 12016 merges the two into one line: '   a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly.'
claim.why_it_matters: Item b) of the by-value matching rules is no longer a list item; its label is swallowed into the text of item a). Any tooling or reader enumerating the conditions of rule 5) sees three subitems (a, c, d) instead of four, and rule 5a now appears to require both the BY VALUE phrase and the OMITTED/OPTIONAL treatment in a single condition. The sibling lists 3) and 4) (lines 11967-11972 and 12006-12012) keep a) and b) separate, confirming the merge is an artifact.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides; I tried to refute it on all four grounds and could not. PDF side - I rendered page 275 (printed folio 245) and page 274 (folio 244) at 300 dpi and additionally crop-zoomed the two page-boundary regions to read the label glyphs directly rather than trusting OCR. * Bottom of page 274, after item '5) For each parameter that is passed by value there shall be a corresponding parameter in the invoked method that:', the last line of the page is a standalone hanging-indent list item whose glyphs I read as lowercase 'a' followed by a closing parenthesis - 'a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase'. The line ends at 'phrase'; there is no continuation text after it and nothing further on the page above the folio line. (Note the sibling items 3a and 4a likewise end without terminal punctuation - 'a) is specified with the BY REFERENCE phrase' - so the absent period is the spec's own house style for this item, not evidence of a run-on.) * Top of page 275, the first body line is a separate hanging-indent list item whose label glyphs I read unambiguously as lowercase 'b' followed by a closing parenthesis - 'b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly.' Its label sits at exactly the same left indentation as the 'c)' item immediately below it and as the 'b)' item of list 4) on page 274, and it is separated from 'c)' by the same inter-item vertical gap used throughout both lists. So the PDF unambiguously prints four sibling items a), b), c), d) under rule 5). Markdown side - line 12016 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md reads verbatim: ' a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly.' The claim quotes it exactly. The next non-blank content is the page-275 marker followed by 'c) ...' at line 12023, so the transcription genuinely presents only three sibling items under rule 5): a), c), d). Why the refutation grounds do not apply: * Not missing text - the b) prose IS present, so this is not a text-loss finding; but the finding as filed is about structure, and the structure IS lost. The label 'b)' has been demoted from a list marker to inline prose in the middle of item a)'s sentence, which is a content change, not a rendering nicety. * Not mere page-break furniture or line wrapping. A pure reflow artifact would join a wrapped continuation of one item; here two DISTINCT numbered items were concatenated, and the enumeration itself was corrupted. The proof that the transcriber's own convention keeps these apart is in the immediately adjacent sibling lists, which I verified: list 3) has 'a) is specified with the BY REFERENCE phrase' on line 11967 and 'b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase...' on line 11969 as separate lines, and list 4) does the same at lines 12006 and 12008 - identical wording, correctly split. Only the instance that straddles the 274/275 page break is merged, which pins the cause to page-boundary stitching. * The claim misquotes neither source (I checked both quotations character-by-character against the render and the file). * Meaning IS changed: read as transcribed, rule 5a states a single conjoined condition, so a conforming implementation could read the OMITTED/OPTIONAL short-circuit ('No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly') as qualifying the BY VALUE requirement of 5a rather than standing as its own independent condition 5b. Cross-references elsewhere in the spec that cite '5a' through '5d' (the by-value analogues of the '4c, 4d, 5c and 5d' citation that appears at line 11955) can no longer be resolved against the transcription's letters. One secondary detail the claim does not mention, which reinforces rather than weakens it: the merged b) text is placed BEFORE the '' marker, so the b) item is additionally mis-attributed to page 274. That is why the per-page work unit for 275 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v275/page-275.md) begins at item c) even though the PDF page begins at item b).
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as filed, with one addition. PDF page 274 (folio 244) ends with the standalone list item 'a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase' under rule 5), and PDF page 275 (folio 245) opens with a separate hanging-indent list item labelled 'b)' - glyphs read directly from the 300 dpi render, at the same indentation as the 'c)' item below it. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 12016 concatenates both onto one line, demoting the 'b)' label to inline prose inside item a) and leaving rule 5) with only three apparent subitems (a, c, d) instead of four. Sibling lists 3) (lines 11967/11969) and 4) (lines 12006/12008) carry the identical a)/b) wording correctly split onto separate lines, so the defect is confined to the instance straddling the 274/275 page break and is a page-boundary stitching artifact. ADDITION: the merged b) text also sits BEFORE the '' marker, so item b) is mis-attributed to page 274 as well as being de-listed - the per-page slice for 275 consequently starts at item c). Fix: split line 12016 after 'is specified with the BY VALUE phrase' and move the resulting 'b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase...' item to just after the page-275 marker, ahead of the existing 'c)' item, matching the indentation used at lines 12006-12012.
